content.text: The cause is confirmed in source: the page-wide definition-list rule wins the CSS cascade (`.workspace-section dl` is more specific than `.decision-metrics`) and turns the three metric cards into a two-column grid. I’m applying a narrowly scoped selector so this component owns both its desktop and mobile layout.

The focused regression test now passes, along with all 40 frontend tests and the production build. Chrome DevTools isn’t available in this workspace, so I’m using the in-app browser testing skill as the runtime fallback to verify the actual wide and narrow layouts against the live local app.
